country.comment: Primary comparative study of Panama and Costa Rica; Tables 5 and 6 also present contextual health and socioeconomic indicators across all 7 Central American countries (Belize, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama).
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title; PDF p. 2, Resumen/Abstract; PDF p. 8, Tables 5-6

effect_estimate.comment: Descriptive cross-national administrative and regulatory comparison; no inferential regression, confidence intervals or p-values are reported. Note minor rounding/denominator variations in text vs. tables (e.g., Costa Rica piped coverage stated as 97.6% in text on pp. 2, 9, 10 and 97.5% in Table 7 on p. 8; total piped including yard pipes is 99.4% in Table 2 on p. 6).
effect_estimate.value: In 2016, Panama achieved 94.6% intradomiciliary piped water coverage (3,819,042 inhabitants) and 74.6% confirmed potable-quality water coverage (2,964,502 urban inhabitants across 130 ASEP-regulated urban aqueducts); water potability is unknown for the 5,619 rural aqueducts (2,836 JAARs and 2,783 Health Committees serving 807,408 inhabitants, 20% of total population) because Technical Regulation DGNTI-COPANIT 23-395-99 and ASEP regulation exclude rural aqueducts (unserved housing shares were highest in indigenous comarcas Embará 72.2%, Ngote Bugle 61.4% and Kuna Yala 22.2%, and provinces Darien 27.4%, Bocas del Toro 25.4% and Veraguas 11.2%). In 2016, Costa Rica achieved 97.6% intradomiciliary piped water coverage (99.4% total piped including yard pipes, 4,861,724 of 4,889,762 inhabitants) and 91.8% potable-quality water coverage (4,487,371 inhabitants; 98% urban and 78.8% rural; 1,988 potable vs. 600 non-potable systems out of 2,588 aqueducts), under nationwide application of Executive Decree N°38924-S and ARESEP regulation of 2,347 aqueducts (excluding 241 municipal systems). Under Costa Rica's Executive Decree N°33953-S-MINAET (PNMSCSAP 2007-2015), potable water coverage increased from 81.2% in 2006 to 91.2% in 2015. No inferential test statistics, 95% CIs or p-values reported.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 2, Resumen/Abstract; PDF pp. 4-6, Resultados & Tables 1-2; PDF pp. 8-11, Table 7, Análisis de Resultados & Conclusiones

mechanism_certainty.comment: Design ceiling for a descriptive comparative legal-institutional study is at most 2. Coded as 1 because the study documents descriptive macro-level correspondences between national regulatory decrees/jurisdictional exclusions (DGNTI-COPANIT 23-395-99 and ASEP urban-only scope in Panama vs. nationwide Decree 38924-S, ARESEP regulation and Decree 33953-S-MINAET in Costa Rica) and aggregate national piped/potable coverage and health statistics, without granular process observation or causal testing.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 3-5, Metodología & Resultados; PDF pp. 9-11, Análisis de Resultados & Conclusiones

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines urban-only vs. nationwide regulatory/surveillance jurisdictional scope (ELIGIBILITY, ENFORCEMENT, service_area: ASEP and DGNTI-COPANIT 23-395-99 excluding Panama's 5,619 rural aqueducts vs. Costa Rica's ARESEP excluding 241 municipal aqueducts and nationwide Decree 38924-S), weak and fragmented sector stewardship (institutional_fragmentation: 'rectoría es débil y fraccionada'), national drinking-water policies and action plans toward 2030 (planning: PNAPS 2017-2030, PNMSCSAP Decree 33953-S-MINAET), inter-institutional sector coordination (political_coordination: CIAPAS, avoiding institutional duplication), and rural community water management organizations (participation: JAARs and Comités de Salud in Panama; CAARs/ASADAS in Costa Rica). Tariffs (fees) appear only as a brief recommendation on p. 12 and were not empirically studied.
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, ENFORCEMENT, service_area, planning, institutional_fragmentation, political_coordination, participation
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 2, Resumen; PDF pp. 4-5, Resultados & Table 2; PDF pp. 9-12, Análisis de Resultados, Conclusiones & Recomendaciones

outcome_flags.comment: Measures household access to drinking water and piped connections (water_access, formal_connection: intradomiciliary/yard piped connections vs. no pipe in Table 4 and text), population service coverage percentages (service_coverage: Tables 1, 2, 7), and microbiological/physicochemical potability plus service quality evaluation via SEECSAP (service_quality: Tables 2, 7 and p. 11). Sanitation is mentioned only qualitatively in discussion without empirical outcome data.
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF p. 2, Resumen; PDF pp. 5-8, Tables 1, 2, 4 & 7; PDF pp. 9-11, Análisis de Resultados & Conclusiones

publication_year.comment: Published in Tecnología en Marcha Vol. 31, N.° 4, Octubre-Diciembre 2018 (approved 9 March 2018).
publication_year.where_found: PDF p. 1, citation block & approval date; PDF pp. 2-13, running header

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Descriptive comparative institutional and regulatory-empirical study combining comparison of water-sector statutes/technical regulations and national policy drafts with aggregate secondary surveillance, census and household survey inventories (no individual-level analytical cross-sectional regression or quasi-experimental comparator). Fits Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework.
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF pp. 3-5, Metodología & Resultados; PDF pp. 9-11, Análisis de Resultados & Conclusiones

sample_size.comment: National administrative, regulatory and household-survey inventories across 2 focal countries (plus 7 Central American countries in health/socioeconomic comparison Tables 5-6). Panama total population is reported as 4,058,372 (Nov 2016 estimate, pp. 3, 10) and 4,037,043 (Table 1, p. 5); rural population served by 5,619 aqueducts is reported as 807,408 (pp. 4, 9) and 807,043 (p. 10).
sample_size.value: 2 countries (Panama and Costa Rica; contextual comparison of 7 Central American countries in Tables 5-6): Panama — 5,749 aqueducts (130 urban; 5,619 rural) and ~4,037,043-4,058,372 inhabitants (plus 5 diagnostic visits); Costa Rica — 2,588 aqueducts (5,312 water sources) and 1,465,259 occupied dwellings / 4,889,762 inhabitants (ENAHO July 2016)
sample_size.where_found: PDF pp. 3-8, Introducción, Metodología & Tables 1-6; PDF pp. 9-11, Análisis de Resultados & Conclusiones

study_design.comment: Authors describe the work as a 'comparative study' / 'comparative analysis' ('estudio comparativo' / 'análisis comparativo'), operationalized via 5 PAHO/OPS diagnostic visits to Panama, descriptive compilation of national water-utility/laboratory surveillance and household-survey inventories (ASEP, DISAPAS, Census 2010, LNA/AyA, INEC ENAHO 2016, PAHO 2015 health indicators), and comparative regulatory/policy review.
study_design.value: Comparative descriptive institutional, regulatory and secondary administrative/surveillance data study (combining 5 diagnostic field visits, national aqueduct/household coverage and water-quality inventories, regional health/socioeconomic indicator comparison, and regulatory/policy document review)
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title; PDF p. 2, Resumen/Abstract; PDF pp. 3-4, Metodología
